item.text: I’m preparing only additional candidates from remembered material, focusing on the body, repair, cornerstone, and mutual-correction images that were absent from the first file. I won’t reopen or check any files.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec12/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.15	bones woven in secret	The commentary joins firm weaving with the meeting of bones; Psalm 139 says the speaker’s bones were not hidden while he was intricately woven, bringing both bodily structure and weaving into one image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.10.11	bones and sinews knit into a body	The commentary treats the meeting of bones as a fitted joint; Job describes God clothing the speaker with skin and flesh and knitting him together with bones and sinews, a distinct image of bodily assembly.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.2.23	bone of my bones	The commentary names the meeting of bones as haqq; the first human recognizes the woman as bone of his bones, making shared bodily substance a kinship image rather than an anatomical junction.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.2.24	cling and become one flesh	The commentary says pieces are joined into a sound whole; Genesis describes two people clinging and becoming one flesh, a relational form of joining that adds kinship to the construction image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.58.12	repairer of the breach	The commentary defines repair as the opposite of corruption; Isaiah calls the restored people repairers of a breach and restorers of streets, making repair both structural and communal.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.147.3	heals broken hearts and binds wounds	The commentary’s salih repairs what is spoiled; the Psalm depicts God healing broken hearts and binding wounds, applying repair directly to damaged persons.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hos.6.1	heals after tearing and binds after striking	The commentary opposes repair to corruption; Hosea calls the people to return because the one who tore them will heal them and bind their wounds, making restoration follow damage.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.18.4	potter reshapes a marred vessel	The commentary says the good work repairs what is spoiled; Jeremiah’s potter reworks a marred vessel into another form, a concrete image of repair through reshaping.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.17	one person sharpens another	The commentary makes mutual counsel join and strengthen separate parts; Proverbs says one person sharpens another as iron sharpens iron, a direct image of reciprocal strengthening.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.2.2	hearts knit together in love	The commentary says mutual advice connects pieces and haqq makes the weave firm; Colossians speaks of hearts knit together in love and reaching full assurance, linking cohesion with shared understanding.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.2.21	whole structure joined and growing into a temple	The commentary fits parts into a secure structure; Ephesians describes the whole building being joined together and growing into a holy temple, an architectural image for a community.
strong	incil	motif	Shepherd of Hermas, Vision 3.2	stones fitted into the tower	The commentary says one piece is joined to another; in the Shepherd’s vision, stones fit together in the tower identified with the Church, giving that connection an early Christian communal interpretation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.28.16	tested stone and firm foundation	The commentary stresses soundness and exact fit; Isaiah describes a tested cornerstone laid as a firm foundation, connecting reliable construction with trust.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.118.22	rejected stone becomes the cornerstone	The commentary’s fitted door and joined structure depend on a sound meeting point; the Psalm’s rejected stone becomes the head of the corner, making a once-discarded piece structurally decisive.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.21.42	rejected stone as cornerstone	Jesus applies the rejected-stone saying to the builders’ judgment of him; this Christian reading of Psalm 118 makes the building image a reversal in which the rejected one becomes structurally central.
medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:1Pet.2.6	Isaiah’s chosen cornerstone applied to Christ	The commentary’s firm fit and foundation imagery meets Peter’s citation of Isaiah’s tested cornerstone as Christ, adding a Christian interpretation in which trust in the chosen stone prevents shame.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.2.17	faith without works is dead	The commentary makes work place bricks and repair what is broken; James insists that faith without works is dead, directly pairing belief with enacted conduct while adding a distinct argument about their necessity.
medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Prov.14.1	wise woman builds; folly tears down	The commentary’s good work repairs and constructs; Proverbs contrasts a wise woman building her house with folly tearing it down, making the same household image express constructive and destructive conduct.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.12.25	divided house cannot stand	The commentary makes counsel join parts into a stable structure; Jesus says a house divided against itself cannot stand, giving disunity the opposite structural consequence.
medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Isa.5.2	cultivated vineyard yields wild grapes	The commentary’s builder and repairer produce a sound moral structure; Isaiah’s owner clears stones, plants a vineyard, and builds its tower, yet receives wild grapes, a crafted project whose result fails its purpose.
medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Isa.5.7	justice expected but bloodshed found	The commentary joins constructive action with haqq; Isaiah identifies the vineyard as Israel and says God expected justice and righteousness but found bloodshed and a cry, making failed ethical fruit the reversal of sound building.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.25	members care for one another without division	The commentary makes counsel connect parts; Paul says the body should have no division and its members should have the same care for one another, giving bodily cohesion a reciprocal ethical consequence.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.49.16	חקק ~ ح ق ق; table’s regular sound correspondence, unverified	Isaiah says Zion is engraved on God’s palms and her walls are continually before him; this possible root correspondence extends the commentary’s firm word and bodily-junction imagery to an enduring inscription, without establishing cognacy.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Babylonian Talmud, Arakhin 16b	reception and giving of rebuke	The commentary’s mutual counsel in truth resembles the command to reprove one’s neighbor; Arakhin discusses how difficult it is both to give and receive rebuke, making reciprocal correction a demanding practice rather than a simple formula.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.2.19	firm foundation paired with turning from iniquity	The commentary opposes sound construction to a weak house and corruption; 2 Timothy says God’s firm foundation stands, then pairs its seal with the command to depart from iniquity, joining structural security to ethical conduct.
EOF"
